run_ref.note: Verdict PASS. Not a re-run for this ask: the archived production run is at a regime that brackets AM's, which is stated as such in `regime`.

claim: For a single-height overdamped harmonic trap in a Newtonian solvent, f_c is recoverable from a finite Brownian trajectory to +1.17 % against a 5 % tolerance at T_obs/tau_k = 2000 with 10 samples per tau_k. Therefore gamma_corr at ONE rung of the ladder is recoverable to that precision from a sufficiently long block, and the per-rung input error of the h0 fit is set by acquisition length, sampling rate and localisation noise -- not by the fit.

answering_quantity.why: NOT the quantity asked for. h0 is unreachable here -- see `gaps`. f_c is the largest sub-question this case can close honestly: it is what sets gamma_corr per rung, and it is the one the archived run actually validated against a closed-form OU solution.

achieved_precision.basis: metrics.json observables[] 'f_c (PSD fit)': measured 40.1516 Hz vs predicted 39.6871 Hz, err_pct +1.1705, tol_pct 5.0. The other four observables of the same run agree to better than 0.35 %.

requirements.from: tau_k = 16.14 ms at your reference rung (derived below, using your declared Faxen factor). T_obs/tau_k = 2000 is the configuration at which this case actually reached f_c to 1.17 %, so 2000 x 16.14 ms = 32.3 s. Your envelope's 5 s gives T_obs/tau_k = 310: that clears this repository's soft floor of 100 (metrics.json checks, non-hard) with margin 3.1, but it is 6.4x below the configuration the 1.17 % was measured at. Nothing here says 310 fails -- it says the 1.17 % does not transfer to it, and no run in this repository has measured what does.

This repository samples at tau_k/10, i.e. f_s = 10/tau_k = 620 Hz at tau_k = 16.14 ms. Your envelope caps f_s at 520 Hz (hard), which is 8.39 samples per tau_k -- 16 % short of the convention, not of a physical limit. Two ways out, both yours to choose: shrink the ROI height (it is what sets your frame rate) or accept 8.39 and treat the Lorentzian corner fit as unvalidated at that sampling. See findings[0]: your own gate asks for f_s >= 10 f_c = 99 Hz, which is 6.28x looser than this because the two conventions differ by 2*pi.

Localisation noise adds in quadrature to the thermal amplitude, so it inflates var(x) by (epsilon/l_k)^2 and deflates the equipartition alpha by the same fraction. l_k = 33.98 nm at your k_t, so a 5 % budget needs epsilon <= 0.2236 l_k = 7.6 nm. Your assumed 10 nm is 0.294 l_k: 8.7 % on var(x) and ~8 % on alpha, which consumes the entire 5 % before the ladder fit starts. This is hard because it does not average away -- it is a bias, not a variance.

Passed through unchanged from your own 400-realisation estimate, NOT independently derived here -- this case has one height and no ladder. Recorded as a requirement so it is visible, and as gaps[2] so it is not read as verified.

regime.name: k*
regime.why_this_tolerance: f_c does not depend on k* alone, and what transfers is the RECOVERABILITY of f_c, which depends on the fit's signal-to-noise through l_k/d. Your k* is 2.84x lower, i.e. this run is the stiffer, harder-to-localise case -- so the 1.17 % transfers conservatively rather than optimistically.

regime.name: l_k/d
regime.tolerance: receiver may be larger, not smaller
regime.why_this_tolerance: Your fluctuation is 1.69x larger relative to the bead than the one validated here, which is the favourable direction for localisation. Had it been smaller the 1.17 % would not have transferred at all.

regime.name: tau_p/tau_k
regime.why_this_tolerance: The hard model check in this repository (metrics.json checks[0], limit 1e-2, margin 12.3 here). Yours is 7.3e-5, margin 137. Overdamped on both sides -- this group is genuinely shared.

regime.name: T_obs/tau_k
regime.why_this_tolerance: The soft check in this repository is >= 100 and yours passes it. But the achieved 1.17 % was measured at 2000, and statistical error on a Lorentzian corner goes as 1/sqrt(T_obs/tau_k): 310 implies roughly sqrt(2000/310) = 2.5x the scatter, i.e. ~3 % rather than ~1.2 %. Still inside 5 %, with almost nothing left for anything else.

regime.name: samples_per_tau_k
regime.why_this_tolerance: Convention inherited from bd-physics, not a derived limit. Stated as a tolerance so the 16 % shortfall is visible; see findings[0] for why the two repositories' numbers differ by 2*pi.

gaps.what: The Faxen separation itself, and therefore h0.
gaps.why: This case has no wall and one height. gamma_0 is bulk Stokes; there is no h in the system at all.
gaps.consequence: The answering quantity you asked for (h0, +/-0.2 um) is NOT answered. This round answers the per-rung input precision that the h0 fit consumes.
gaps.would_need: A runner for a trapped sphere at a no-slip wall with a height-dependent mobility. RUNNERS in cli.py has one card today (passive-sphere--harmonic-trap); this would be a second one, and running the trap runner on it would silently compute the wrong system.

gaps.why: A BD trajectory has no detector. Adding both is a post-processing layer over the sampled positions, not a change of physics -- so it is cheap, but it does not exist yet.
gaps.consequence: The 1.17 % is a noise-free number. Your requirement epsilon <= 7.6 nm was derived analytically here, not simulated.
gaps.would_need: A sampling layer: integrate positions over t_exp, then add Gaussian epsilon. Roughly a day, and it would let the next round answer the question this one deferred.

gaps.what: The six-rung least-squares fit for h0 and gamma_bulk.
gaps.why: No ladder was simulated. requirements[3] passes your own 3 %/rung figure through unchanged.
gaps.consequence: sigma_gamma_per_rung <= 3 % is recorded but unverified. Do not read it as corroborated.
gaps.would_need: The wall runner above, plus a synthetic ladder at six heights x the seed count.

gaps.why: N = 1000 was chosen as a statistics device and settled confirmed_by: run.
gaps.consequence: Every error bar in this document is an ensemble error bar. The experiment has one bead per rung.
gaps.would_need: Re-run at n_replicas = 1 with many seeds and report the per-realisation scatter. Cheap; should be the first thing the next round does.

findings.what: The two repositories' sampling conventions differ by exactly 2*pi.
findings.am_says: f_s >= 10 f_c (gate sampling.aliased / G14c). At f_c = 9.9 Hz that is 99 Hz, and 520 fps clears it 5.3x.
findings.bd_says: sample interval = tau_k/10, i.e. f_s = 10/tau_k = 62.8 f_c = 620 Hz. 520 fps is 16 % short.

findings.what: The localisation-noise budget is already spent at the assumed epsilon.
findings.am_says: epsilon = 10 nm is ~9 % of var(x); measure it on a stuck bead (P8) and correct for it.
findings.bd_says: 8 % on alpha is a bias, not a variance, and it does not average down over rungs or segments. A 5 % budget needs epsilon <= 7.6 nm; correcting for a measured epsilon is fine, but the correction's own error then becomes the budget.

findings.what: 5 s per rung is 6.4x below the configuration the 1.17 % was measured at.
findings.am_says: 3 segments x 5 s per velocity, plus 5 s of held bead at step 9c, chosen against a ~15-independent-samples-per-plateau argument.
findings.bd_says: T_obs/tau_k = 310 versus the validated 2000. Passes the soft floor of 100; implies ~3 % rather than ~1.2 % on f_c, leaving almost nothing for the epsilon bias above.

findings.what: The error bars in this document are ensemble error bars.
findings.am_says: (not addressed -- the ask did not distinguish)
findings.bd_says: N = 1000 independent replicas. One bead would scatter ~32x more at the same T_obs/tau_k. Any comparison of this 1.17 % against a single-bead measurement is invalid as stated.
